page: Microsoft Azure E128-32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by AMD EPYC 9V45 processors utilizing x86_64 architecture, providing 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating up to 4.5 GHz. The platform features an extensive cache configuration consisting of 48 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster. Complementing the processor cores is 1024.0 GB of system memory, delivering an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU. The instance also bundles 7560 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and includes no GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight strong computational capabilities, particularly in single-threaded metrics and specialized instruction execution. Single-core performance ranks in the top tier on both stress-ng (3787.49) and Geekbench (2884.0), corroborated by top-tier single-threaded compression throughputs such as 41.3 GB/sec in gzip. Geekbench multi-core performance reaches 22126.0, ranking in the top tier alongside software compilation (41111.0) and image processing (22423.0). Memory throughput is stable, yielding 101.48 GB/sec in uncached 256MB read operations and 67.44 GB/sec in uncached write operations, while PassMark tests record strong overall CPU and memory marks.

Architecturally, the server provides substantial memory capacity alongside constrained compute resources, representing a constrained-vCPU profile tailored for memory-bound applications. The inclusion of 7560 GB local NVMe SSD storage minimizes dependency on external storage volumes for caching and temporary storage. While lightweight LLM inference runs capably—generating 390.7 tokens/sec on small 135M models—larger models such as 70B show severe degradation (2.44 tokens/sec) due to lack of hardware accelerators. Tradeoffs include average multi-threaded stress performance and database transaction rates compared to fully allocated multi-socket setups.

The Microsoft Azure E128-32ads_v7 is tailored for workloads requiring vast RAM and low CPU licensing footprints. Prime use cases encompass large in-memory databases like SAP HANA or Redis, large-scale ETL data transformation, enterprise memory-resident analytics, and heavy compiler or rendering workloads that leverage large working memory datasets.
